subject: chemistry
title: Extracting aluminium by electrolysis
key_idea: Metals that are more reactive than carbon cannot be extracted by heating with carbon, so they are extracted by electrolysis of a molten compound. Aluminium is made from molten aluminium oxide mixed with cryolite. The process uses a lot of energy.

blocks.text: This section covers which metals are extracted by electrolysis and why.

items: A metal that is **less reactive than carbon**, such as iron or copper, can be extracted by heating its oxide with carbon.
A metal that is **more reactive than carbon**, such as aluminium, cannot be reduced by carbon. Its oxide is very stable.
A metal that reacts with carbon cannot be extracted with carbon either.
These metals are extracted by electrolysis of a molten compound. Calcium is another example.
The metal made by electrolysis is very pure.
Large amounts of energy are used to melt the compounds and to produce the electric current.
So electrolysis is more expensive than heating with carbon.
Extracting aluminium costs more than extracting iron, because it uses more energy.
Metals more reactive than carbon, or that react with carbon, are extracted by electrolysis.
Electrolysis uses a lot of energy to melt the compound and to supply the current.

blocks.text: This section covers the electrolyte, the electrodes and the reactions in the aluminium cell.

items.meaning: A compound mixed with aluminium oxide to lower the melting point of the electrolyte.

items: The electrolyte is a molten mixture of **aluminium oxide** and **cryolite**.
Aluminium oxide alone melts at 2045 °C. The mixture melts at 950 °C.
The lower melting point means less energy is needed to melt the electrolyte.
The positive electrode (anode) is made of carbon (graphite).
Aluminium ions are positive, so they are attracted to the negative electrode. Aluminium forms there.
Oxide ions are negative, so they are attracted to the positive electrode. Oxygen forms there.

blocks.label: Electrolysis of aluminium oxide
where: Al is aluminium, made at the negative electrode
O₂ is oxygen, made at the positive electrode

items: (Higher tier) Negative electrode: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. The aluminium ions gain electrons.
(Higher tier) Positive electrode: 2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻. The oxide ions lose electrons.

blocks.text: Why the positive electrodes are replaced

diagram.alt: Why the carbon positive electrodes must be replaced in the extraction of aluminium.
steps: Oxygen forms at the positive electrode
At a high temperature, the oxygen reacts with the carbon electrode
The electrode burns away and must be replaced

items: Cryolite lowers the melting point of aluminium oxide, so less energy is used.
Aluminium forms at the negative electrode and oxygen at the positive electrode.
Oxygen reacts with the carbon electrode to make carbon dioxide, so the electrodes are replaced.

checks.q: Explain why aluminium is extracted by electrolysis and not by heating with carbon.
checks.a: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot remove the oxygen from aluminium oxide.

checks.q: Why is cryolite added to aluminium oxide?
checks.a: The mixture has a lower melting point than aluminium oxide, so less energy is needed.

checks.q: Explain why the positive carbon electrodes must be continually replaced.
checks.a: Oxygen is produced at the positive electrode. It reacts with the carbon to form carbon dioxide, so the electrode burns away.

exam_phrases: metal is too reactive to be extracted using carbon
the mixture has a lower melting point (than aluminium oxide)
(so the electrode) has to be continually replaced
aluminium ions are positive(ly charged) so are attracted to the negative electrode

mistakes.wrong: Cryolite is added as a catalyst.
mistakes.right: This is not accepted. Cryolite lowers the melting point of the mixture, so less energy is needed.

mistakes.wrong: A lower melting point means the process costs less.
mistakes.right: Cost is ignored. Say that less energy is needed.

mistakes.wrong: The molten mixture contains bauxite and cryolite.
mistakes.right: Bauxite and aluminium ore are ignored. The molten mixture contains aluminium oxide and cryolite.
Corroded is ignored in some questions. Say that the carbon electrode reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide, so it burns away or is used up.

worked_example.question:
This question is about the extraction of aluminium.

Oxygen is formed at the positive carbon electrodes.

Explain why the positive carbon electrodes must be continually replaced.
answer_points: At a high temperature, oxygen reacts with the carbon (electrode).
So the positive electrode burns away.
worked_example.tip: The equation C + O₂ → CO₂ scores the first and third marks.

mistakes.wrong: Aluminium is more reactive, so it is extracted by electrolysis.

This repeats the question and is ignored. Explain why: aluminium oxide cannot be reduced by carbon.

mistakes.wrong: Electrolysis is used for iron because it is cheaper than heating with carbon.
mistakes.right: Electrolysis is more expensive. Iron is extracted by heating with carbon because iron is less reactive than carbon.

worked_example.question:
Metals can be extracted from ores found in the Earth's crust.

Explain why aluminium cannot be extracted from its ore by heating with carbon but can be extracted by electrolysis.
answer_points: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon (so electrolysis is required).
Carbon cannot remove the oxygen. There is no reaction between carbon and aluminium oxide, or carbon cannot displace aluminium.
Electrolysis can be used to reduce aluminium ions.
worked_example.tip: Electrolysis is a more powerful method of reduction is also allowed.

exam_phrases: aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series
so cannot be obtained by reaction of oxide with carbon
copper is below carbon in the reactivity series
aluminium is highly / too / very reactive

mistakes.wrong: Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis because it is reactive.
mistakes.right: 'Reactive' or 'quite reactive' is ignored. Say that aluminium is more reactive than carbon, or above carbon in the reactivity series.

mistakes.wrong: Solid aluminium oxide cannot be electrolysed because its electrons cannot move.
mistakes.right: Electrons cannot move is ignored. Say that the ions cannot move in the solid.

worked_example.question:
Aluminium is extracted from its ore using electrolysis.

Copper is extracted from its ore by heating with carbon.

Explain why different methods are used to extract aluminium and copper.
answer_points: Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, so it cannot be obtained by reaction of its oxide with carbon.
Copper is below carbon in the reactivity series.
